title: PhysVista: Benchmarking Physical Intelligence in VLMs via a Perception-Reasoning-Assessment Loop
claim: A benchmark is organized into a taxonomy of capabilities, staged into a perception-reasoning-assessment loop, and used to compare many models.
layout: Left radial taxonomy wheel; right three stacked stage panels above radar charts
description: The figure has two halves inside a dashed yellow border. The left half is a large circular sunburst chart with four quadrants. Perception is green, Reasoning is blue, Assessment is purple, and Physical Principle and Video Scenario are yellow and orange. Inner rings give the main categories, such as Spatial, Uncertainty, Causality, Temporal, Scoring and Comparison. Outer rings give subtask labels, such as Camera Motion, Counterfactual, Gen vs. Gen, Buoyancy, Friction, Water and Metal. The right half has three horizontal stage panels: I. Seeing in blue, II. Reasoning in green, and III. Assessment in red. Each panel shows a robot or brain icon, video frame strips, and small task icons. Two radar charts sit at the bottom. They compare about 15 VLMs, with a legend on the right. The eye goes first to the colorful wheel.
caption: Overview of PhysVista. PhysVista evaluates physical intelligence in VLMs through Seeing, Reasoning, and Assessment across real and generated videos.
abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong multimodal reasoning capabilities, yet whether they truly capture the physical consistency underlying real-world dynamics remains unclear. Existing benchmark paradigms often suffer from fragmented evaluation, focusing on isolated cognitive stages while overlooking the inherent synergy between perception, reasoning, and physical judgment. The lack of a holistic perspective limits the ability to diagnose whether VLMs can reliably serve as evaluators of physical plausibility in generative content. To address these issues, we introduce PhysVista, a benchmark designed to evaluate physical intelligence in VLMs through a closed cognitive loop framework inspired by the human seeing-reasoning-assessment process. PhysVista restores this loop by jointly evaluating physical state perception, physical dynamics reasoning, and physical plausibility assessment. It further distinguishes event-level reasoning and scale-level reasoning to enable fine-grained analysis of physical understanding. In addition, PhysVista incorporates both real-world and AI-generated videos, allowing evaluation across diverse domains and emerging generative scenarios. Extensive experiments across a diverse set of VLMs reveal substantial limitations in physical reasoning and plausibility assessment, highlighting a persistent gap between visual recognition and genuine physical understanding, and pointing toward more principled designs for physically grounded multimodal intelligence.
